Recombine diverse annealed optima by Hungarian+Procrustes alignment and great-sphere splicing with void repair.
direction: Build and recombine a population of distinct local optima: generate 6–10 codes by strong kicks and annealing even if their scores are only in the 0.905–0.93 range, and retain diversity by comparing their contact graphs rather than keeping near-duplicates of the record. For pairs of parents, align them by alternating Hungarian assignment on pairwise inner products with orthogonal Procrustes alignment over $O(4)$, including reflections; then splice the aligned codes along several random great spheres, taking complementary hemispherical subsets with the boundary adjusted to retain exactly 272 points. Repair the closest cross-boundary pairs by void reinsertion, anneal and LP-polish the children, and iterate using the best and most graph-diverse offspring while always retaining the original record as a safe fallback.

idea: Continuation in N around the jammed optimum — overshoot to 280-288 via largest-void insertion and reoptimize then prune worst-burden points back to 272, plus the reverse undershoot to 248-256 and greedy void reinsertion, each with soft-max repulsion and trust-region LP polishing.
direction: Use continuation in the number of points to move around the jam globally: overshoot to $N=280$–$288$ by inserting points into the largest voids of the record and fully reoptimizing, forcing the entire 272-point core to redistribute, then repeatedly delete the point with the largest worst-contact burden and re-polish after each deletion until returning to 272. Also run the reverse path from the other side—delete 16–24 points, thoroughly reoptimize the looser $N=248$–$256$ code, and reinsert points one at a time using largest-void placement plus global re-polishing—using several deletion orders and random seeds. This changes the problem’s constraint-to-degree-of-freedom balance along the path, allowing the final 272-point configuration to approach the target from a different basin rather than trying to cross the barrier at fixed $N$.

idea: Large patch surgery around hubs plus rattlers with frozen-core sequential void refill and anneal/LP re-jam.
direction: Perform large contact-graph surgery instead of deleting only two to four offenders: construct the contact graph at slack $10^{-7}$–$10^{-6}$, select a connected BFS or spectral community of about 24–40 points around a highly contacted point, delete that whole patch together with the three rattlers, and freeze the remaining core. Refill the cavity sequentially, placing each point initially at the best of at least 20,000 random sphere samples measured against the frozen core plus already inserted points, locally optimizing each insertion, and then unfreeze everything for a short high-temperature log-sum-exp phase followed by LP polishing. Cycle through several distinct communities and patch sizes, accepting intermediate configurations based partly on contact-graph change—not solely immediate score—so the final LP polish can settle into a genuinely different jam.

idea: Large-patch cap surgery with greedy farthest-point reinsertion and two-stage anneal plus LP polish under count-aware simulated annealing.
direction: Implement large-patch delete-and-reinsert surgery instead of global kicks: repeatedly pick a random unit vector $u$, delete the $k\in\{24,36,48\}$ points with largest $\langle x_i,u\rangle$ plus the 3 rattlers, freeze the remaining points, and rebuild the deleted points greedily from a pool of $\sim$40000 random unit vectors by successively choosing candidates that maximise their minimum distance to frozen plus already-reinserted points, followed by local tangential optimisation of only the inserted points against the frozen set. Then unfreeze all points, run a short log-sum-exp anneal and the existing LP polish, and accept the result by simulated annealing using the number of pairs above $0.8975$ as well as the max cosine. Cycle through different caps and values of $k$ for $\sim$120 seconds, always keeping the best configuration found as fallback.

idea: Lexicographic slack attack with thresholded squared-softplus surrogates plus Riemannian Adam and interleaved LP squeeze
direction: Attack the pair-slack spectrum lexicographically rather than the max alone: define thresholds $t\in\{0.8980,0.8975,0.8970,0.8965\}$ and, with Riemannian Adam or L-BFGS on the sphere, minimise a smooth hinge objective $\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{softplus}((\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-t)/\tau)^2$ with $\tau\sim10^{-4}$, whose purpose is to reduce the count of pairs above $t$ and push down the second tier visible at slack $10^{-6}$–$10^{-2}$, even if the max temporarily rises slightly. Alternate each surrogate stage with LP polish, record the full histogram of pair cosines after each stage, and retain configurations that reduce the number of contacts within $10^{-4}$ of the max while keeping the max below $0.8985$, since a sparser near-contact set is what can later let the LP drop below the record.

idea: Cyclic 16- and 8-fold diagonal rotation orbits with L-BFGS on log-sum-exp then symmetry-broken anneal and LP polish
direction: Build fresh configurations from symmetry-group orbits, ignoring the record except as fallback: use rotations by multiples of $2\pi/m$ simultaneously in the $(x_1,x_2)$ and $(x_3,x_4)$ planes to generate orbits of size 8, 16, or 17-point unions totalling 272, parameterise only the orbit representatives (e.g. 17 representatives of 16-point orbits, or 34 of 8-point orbits, each represented by two radii and two angles), and optimise the representatives with L-BFGS on a log-sum-exp surrogate with $\tau$ annealed from $0.02$ to $0.001$. Then break the symmetry gradually: expand to the full 272 points, add tangential noise of size $10^{-3}$, $10^{-2}$, and $3\times10^{-2}$ in separate branches, anneal and LP-polish each branch, and keep the best. This searches an entirely different basin with a built-in balanced contact structure.

Escape the over-jammed amorphous basin by searching de novo from balanced Hopf-fiber symmetric constructions plus random Riesz-energy starts with hybrid Riesz-to-softmax Adam annealing, then LP-polish the best new basins.

Search cyclic orbit basins with 8 seeds times 34 double-plane rotations for several coprime multipliers, Adam-optimizing seeds on sharpened log-sum-exp then breaking symmetry to full points with anneal and LP polish.
direction: Search a completely different, symmetry-generated basin using orbit codes under simultaneous rotations in two orthogonal planes: take eight generic seed points in $\mathbb R^4$, generate 34 rotated copies of each by rotating the first coordinate plane through $2\pi j/34$ and the second through $2\pi qj/34$, for $j=0,\ldots,33$ and several multipliers $q$ coprime to 34, producing exactly $8\times34=272$ points from only 32 seed coordinates. Optimize the seeds with Adam or L-BFGS on a sharpening log-sum-exp objective, scanning several random seed sets and $q$ values, then gradually break the symmetry by allowing first seed-block displacements and finally independent point displacements before LP polishing. Even if the symmetric optimum is slightly worse, its contact graph will be far more equitable and may lie in a better basin after symmetry breaking than the amorphous record configuration.

idea: Rebalance the over-jammed contact network by jointly deleting hub-plus-rattler neighbourhood patches into greedy voids and re-annealing with alternating hinge and log-sum-exp Adam plus LP snap.
Break the over-jammed basin with rigidity-guided topology moves that pin one hub contact below the maximum and relocate rattlers to hub centroids before annealing and constrained LP polish.
direction: Use rigidity analysis to force specific topology changes: form the rigidity matrix of the $\sim$820 contacts in tangent coordinates, compute per-point contact degrees and local stress via the left null space (self-stress) using a sparse SVD, then enumerate targeted moves that break one chosen hub contact by adding the explicit constraint $\langle x_i,x_j\rangle\le M-2\times10^{-4}$ for a degree-$\ge$8 pair to the LP while minimising $t$ over all other near-maximal pairs. In parallel, relocate each rattler to the normalised centroid direction of a hub's contact neighbourhood (the point a rattler could "support"), displace the hub tangentially by $0.02$–$0.05$, anneal briefly, and LP-polish. Iterate over the top $\sim$30 hub contacts and all rattlers, keeping any polished result whose contact graph has lower degree variance at equal max cosine as the new starting point for further cycles.

idea: Lexicographic hinge-plus-balance attack with cyclic thresholded squared-softplus Riemannian Adam, hub/rattler-targeted kicks and void reinsertion, interleaved with trust-region LP squeeze.

idea: Frozen-core rattler surgery fixing hubs with >=6 contacts and jointly reoptimizing rattlers plus low-contact points and their >0.75 neighbours via void plus equidistant seeding and annealed smooth-max L-BFGS feasibility tests before global anneal and LP polish.
direction: Perform frozen-core rattler surgery rather than moving all 272 points: freeze every point with at least six contacts, and jointly reoptimize only the three rattlers, all points with at most four contacts, and their neighbours among pairs with cosine above $0.75$, typically a 25–45 point subproblem. For each rattler, generate candidate positions from dense random samples, local spherical Voronoi vertices, and points approximately equidistant from four nearby frozen points, then use SLSQP or a small LP sequence to test feasibility at target cosines $0.8975$, $0.8970$, and $0.8965$ for moved–moved and moved–frozen pairs. Accept a surgery only if a rattler gains at least three near-contacts without creating a pair above the record, unfreeze progressively larger neighbourhoods if infeasible, and finish with the ordinary LP polish; this directly attacks the wasted degrees of freedom instead of shaking the rigid core.

idea: Force contact-topology changes along LP-dual stress directions with penalized high-stress contacts, over-stepped line search and exclusion re-polish scored lexicographically.
direction: Use LP dual variables to force a contact-topology change: solve the final trust-region LP, rank active contacts by their inequality dual multipliers, select 20–40 high-stress contacts that do not all share one hub, and resolve a modified LP in which those selected cosines are constrained to be at most $t-\delta$ for $\delta\in\{10^{-4},3\times10^{-4},10^{-3},3\times10^{-3}\}$ while all other near-contacts remain at most $t$. Take the resulting displacement well beyond the usual trust-region step by line-searching multiples $1,2,4,8,16$ of it, project back to the sphere, and re-polish with the selected contacts initially excluded from the active set. Score trials lexicographically by maximum cosine, then number of pairs within $10^{-6}$ of that maximum, then the sum of the largest 100 cosines, and retain non-worsening topology changes for several rounds; this searches along stress-bearing constraints that ordinary LP polishing only reinforces.

idea: Escape the over-jammed basin by coordinated patch surgery around overloaded hubs and rattlers with greedy void refilling and balanced annealed repulsion, then trust-region LP polish.
